## Overview

LRP107 is the suite's first **speech-production-exposure** mechanism model. It estimates
the adjusted association between speech production (`deapp_c`) and **nonword decoding**
across *all three phase transitions* (t1$\to$t2, t2$\to$t3, t3$\to$t4) with
phase-specific intercepts (#421 Tier 1). Under the revised DAG (2026-07-10) speech
production is a parent of both letter sounds and nonword decoding
($SP \to \{TE, EV, LS, PA, NW\}$), and the letter-sound $\to$ word-reading review found
it a consistent discriminator of word reading *among children alike on letter sounds*
(+0.19 to +0.28 across waves) — yet no SP-exposure mechanism existed. This fits the
adjusted $SP \to N$ dose-response — *"is clearer speech associated with more nonwords
read?"*

_Covariate exposure (estimand note)._ The exposure is the speech-accuracy covariate
`deapp_c`, which has no bounded-count denominator, so it enters as a **standardised
continuous covariate**: $\beta_{\text{mech}}$ is the adjusted association per **+1 SD of
the observed measure** (the raw-scale SD is recorded in `config.json` as
`mechanism_exposure_sd_raw`). Rows where speech production was not measured are
**dropped**, not imputed. The mechanism is necessarily **linear** — a single slope, not
a shape.

_Floored outcome (linear, not HSGP)._ As `mech-106`, nonword reading is a 6-item count
heavily floored at zero, so a nonparametric age dose-response is not identifiable; the
exposure enters linearly and the outcome is the graded Beta-Binomial on the nonword
count, conditioning on its own baseline $N_{\text{pre}}$.

## Adjustment set

Measured parents of $SP$ under the revised DAG: $\{A, GA, HS\}$.

- $G$ — group; always conditioned on via $\beta_G$.
- $A$ — age; conditioned on linearly (a $\gamma_A\,z(\text{age})$ term).
- $HS$ — hearing status (`hs` / `hs_missing`), $SP$'s measured parent; blocks the
  $SP \leftarrow HS \to \{\dots\} \to N$ route at its root.
- $N_{\text{pre}}$ — baseline nonword decoding (temporal precedence; not a collider).

$LS$ and $PA$ lie on mediating routes from $SP$ to $N$ ($SP \to LS \to N$,
$SP \to PA \to N$); conditioning on them would block legitimate indirect paths and pull
the slope toward the direct-only component, so they are **not** in the adjustment set.
$GA$ (general ability) is latent and cannot be conditioned on; the child random
intercept proxies its time-invariant part, so the slope stays an **adjusted association,
never causal**. The DAG has no $IG \to SP$ or $IS \to SP$ edge, so there is no
session-dose backdoor.

### Interpretation caveats

- *No unmeasured confounder assumption* for $(SP_{\text{post}}, N_{\text{post}})$: strong and not testable — latent general ability is only partially proxied by the child intercept.
- Speech production is measured with error; non-negligible error attenuates the slope toward zero.
- Dropping unmeasured-exposure rows assumes the missingness is unrelated to the association being estimated (missing-at-random given the adjusters); the fitted row count is reported in `config.json`.
- The heavy nonword-reading floor limits outcome variance in the early waves; across-phase pooling assumes a stable structural relationship (a phase-specific sensitivity fit is available via the `phase_specific_mechanism` flag).
